claims.claim: Jiang says New Zealand, Australia, and Canada are not true nation-states but resource colonies of the British Empire whose wealth and political structure remain subordinated to British interests.
He predicts New Zealand is unlikely to join major wars directly, but its population will be replaced through immigration and this will likely produce civil conflict under conditions of decline.
claims.temporal_scope: Political and demographic prediction stated on 2026-05-28.

claims.claim: Jiang says his late twenties were marked by depression and hopelessness, and he treats that descent as a necessary stage that forces people into self-reflection rather than something to avoid at all costs.
He says Yale left him with a naive meritocratic worldview, and his later failures pushed him to build a more nuanced picture of how power and success actually work.
Jiang names Dante's Divine Comedy as the work that most influenced him over the past ten to twenty years and links it to his attempt to guide others into deeper self-reflection about purpose.
He agrees that true scientific innovation is occult in character because major inventors and heroic founders act as if they are on a mission from God to transform the world.

Jiang says free will makes both good and evil technological projects possible, but the innovators most likely to succeed historically are those aligned with power, control, and money rather than service to humanity.
claims.temporal_scope: Historical and theological model stated on 2026-05-28.

claims.claim: He argues that history has a directional bias toward power, which is why figures like Zuckerberg, Jobs, and Ellison become more successful than teachers oriented toward educating people.

signature_moments.moment: New Zealand, Australia, and Canada are collapsed into one imperial category: not sovereign nations but British resource colonies.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they're not nation states they are resource colonies of the British Empire
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's most forceful geopolitical recoding and likely a reusable lens pressure point.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns his own depression into a threshold event that shattered meritocratic faith and launched the inquiry that produced his present worldview.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I thought the world was meritocratic
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the lecture a rare autobiographical origin story instead of abstract diagnosis alone.

signature_moments.moment: The heroic innovator is described as someone convinced he is on a secret mission from God and must build a movement around himself to advance humanity.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they are on a mission a secret mission from God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This crystallizes Jiang's link between occult aspiration, charismatic founding, and technological history.

signature_moments.moment: History is pictured as a current flowing toward power, rewarding those who love money and domination more than those who want to help humanity.
signature_moments.source_phrase: there's almost like a direction to history
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses his theology of free will into a brutal success filter for modern technological civilization.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for New Zealand, Australia, and Canada as territories whose resources and wealth remain effectively owned by the British imperial system rather than by sovereign national communities.
The period of questioning assumptions that Jiang says followed his depression and allowed him to reorient his life toward deeper purpose.
Not just hidden ritual but the imaginative and spiritually charged drive behind genuine innovation, heroic ambition, and world-shaping technological projects.

chronology_notes.note: This dated 2026-05-28 source includes an explicit autobiographical sequence: Yale meritocracy, depressive collapse in Jiang's late twenties, self-reflection, then the intellectual path that produced his current teaching project.
Within the final-exam lecture, Jiang explicitly folds his earlier Holy Empire of AI interpretation into a broader historical-theological account of innovation, occult knowledge, and power.

uncertainty_notes.note: The New Zealand question and answer contain noisy ASR around war references and migration counts, so the packet preserves the stable geopolitical thrust without overfitting every noun.
Several phrases in the free-will and technology section are damaged by ASR, but the contrast between humanitarian intent and power-oriented success remains clear.
